title: About
text:
Dr. Katerina G. Tsakiri is a computational statistician and data scientist specializing in machine learning and AI methods for the physical sciences. Her expertise covers time series decomposition, signal extraction from high-noise data, neural networks, and hybrid statistical and machine learning forecasting models, with applications in atmospheric science, hydrology, volcanology, and climate-related hazards. She has developed novel methodologies and open-source tools, including the R package sima for detecting weak signals in environmental monitoring data, and her recent work integrates classical time series techniques with modern machine learning approaches. She is passionate about interdisciplinary training of the next generation of data scientists, using AI in teaching and research.
She is Associate Professor of Management Science and Chair of the Department of Information Systems, Analytics & Supply Chain Management at the Norm Brodsky College of Business, Rider University, and Founding Director of Rider’s Risk Management and Insurance Certificate Program. In 2026 she co-authored the book R for Earth and Sustainability Data Analytics with Dr. Antonios E. Marsellos.

title: Leadership & Service
text:
Since Fall 2021, Chair of the Department of Information Systems, Analytics & Supply Chain Management at the Norm Brodsky College of Business, Rider University, providing academic and administrative leadership for a multidisciplinary unit spanning Business Analytics, Information Technology Management, and Supply Chain Management.

Lead unit-level academic planning aligned with enrollment trends, workforce needs, and institutional priorities
Oversee faculty workload distribution, instructional coverage, and course scheduling
Recruit, hire, mentor, and evaluate tenure-track and adjunct faculty; manage onboarding and faculty development
Oversee departmental budget planning and resource allocation
Contribute to AACSB accreditation through assessment planning, curriculum mapping, and continuous improvement

title: Research Areas
text:
My research develops statistical and machine learning methods for the physical sciences. The methods come first: time series decomposition, signal extraction from high-noise data, and hybrid statistical and machine learning forecasting. Air quality, floods, groundwater, volcanoes, and climate-related hazards are the applications, and recent work brings the same methods into business analytics education.
